name: S-Class Intern
body:
An s-class intern is the best person for the job willing to work for the experience alone. In a gig economy, interning is as popular as it gets when it comes to learning the ins and outs of adventuring. Sure, most of your companions act like they’re better than you, and yeah, you’re probably not getting credit for killing that goblin at 2 in the morning before it could ambush your drunken wizard who walked away from the camp to relieve himself, but at least you’re coming out of this with some top recommendations for a party of your own. Right?

Role: An s-class intern’s role is as nebulous as it is vague and ill-defined.

Note: The s-class intern is an alternate, superior version of the intern class, which is an alternate, superior version of the unchained rogue class, which is an alternate, superior version of the Pathfinder 1e rogue class, which is an alternate, superior version of the D&D 3.5 rogue class, which is an alternate… Okay, I think you get the point. They retain all of the standard intern progressions and options, and as such should qualify to select intern archetypes without specific adjustments.

Alignment: Any, but usually naive and good intentioned.

Hit Die: d8.

Starting Wealth: How about you tell me what you should start with, and we can laugh about it around the water cooler. What’s a water cooler doing in this obviously fantasy world of dragons and wizards, you ask? You’ll find out when (if?) we hire you full time, which will be any day now… Oh, but I guess you should begin play with an outfit worth 10 gp or less. We’re not heartless, afterall. Just, soulless.

Class Skills

The s-class intern’s class skills are Acrobatics (Dex), Appraise (Int), Autohypnosis (Wis), Bluff (Cha), Climb (Str), Craft (Int), Diplomacy (Cha), Disable Device (Dex), Disguise (Cha), Escape Artist (Dex), Fly (Dex), Handle Animal (Cha), Heal (Wis), Intimidate (Cha), Knowledge (arcana) (Int), Knowledge (dungeoneering) (Int), Knowledge (engineering) (Int), Knowledge (geography) (Int), Knowledge (history) (Int), Knowledge (nature) (Int), Knowledge (nobility) (Int), Knowledge (planes) (Int), Knowledge (religion) (Int), Linguistics (Int), Perception (Wis), Perform (Cha), Profession (Wis), Ride (Dex), Sense Motive (Wis), Sleight of Hand (Dex), Spellcraft (Int), Stealth (Dex), Survival (Wis), Swim (Str), and Use Magic Device (Cha).

Skill Ranks per Level: 8 + Int modifier.

Class Features

All of the following are class features of the s-class intern.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency

S-class interns are proficient with all weapons, all armor, and all shields (except tower shields). Wait, wait. I worry what you just read was, ‘… are proficient with simple and martial weapons; light, medium, and heavy armor.’ What I wrote was, ‘… are proficient with all weapons and armor that a character can be proficient with.’ Do you understand?

Follow the Lead

An s-class intern is there to learn the job, particularly when it comes to being an adventurer. When an ally the intern can see and hear succeeds at an attack roll, ability check, skill check, or saving throw, the intern can apply that ally’s bonus (including any penalties) to his own ability modifier as a free action when attempting the same task before the end of his next turn. This does not grant the intern benefits or penalties beyond the bonus itself—such as extra damage dealt with Power Attack, or a penalty to AC when charging or using Cleave—unless he also has the ability or uses the same action.

For example, if Bud the barbarian rages and attacks an alce with Power Attack, his bonus to hit becomes 8 + his Strength modifier. If his attack hits and Tony the intern can see him do it, Tony’s next attack is made at 8 + his ability modifier, but he gains none of the other penalties or benefits such as increased damage. If Tony also has Power Attack, he gains the appropriate bonus to damage for his level without also subtracting from his attack roll (since Bud’s 2 attack already did that).

On-the-Job Training (Ex)

At 1st level, and again at 11th and 20th level, an s-class intern is better able to protect himself when he can’t rely on an ally to do so. He gains a +2 competence bonus on two different saves of his choice between Fortitude, Reflex, or Will. These bonuses stack with themselves.

Pay (Ex)

An s-class intern begins play with no promise of pay, represented on Table: S-Class Intern as a hyphen. While adventuring, the intern doesn’t count towards party treasure rewards. In a group of 5 with an intern, the GM is strongly encouraged to build treasure rewards for a group of 4 instead. To keep things balanced, of course.

This doesn’t prevent a party from offering to share their loot with the intern, but they should be aware that doing so could lead to raised hopes and a sense of accomplishment.

At 8th level, an s-class intern’s pay is represented by an en dash, instead. At 14th level, it is represented by an em dash.

At 20th level, an s-class intern’s pay reaches its peak at 0 gp. A mythic s-class intern’s pay becomes zilch instead, and an epic s-class intern’s pay is nada.

Team Fit

Every intern hopes to get picked for the perfect adventuring group. To do so, they strive to learn complimentary skills. At 1st level, an s-class intern gains a competence bonus equal to half his intern level (minimum 1) plus his Wisdom modifier (if positive) on untrained skill checks when he makes those checks alone.

Trapfinding (Ex)

An s-class intern adds half his level on Perception checks to locate traps and on Disable Device checks (minimum +1).

An s-class intern can use Disable Device to disarm magic traps.

Build Competency (Ex)

At 2nd level, and every even level thereafter, an s-class intern can choose 1 class skill he possesses, other than Disable Device, Knowledge (local), and Perception. He gains a competency bonus on checks made with that skill equal to half his intern level.

At 12th level, and every even level thereafter, an s-class intern can instead choose a skill in which he already has build competency. He gains the skill unlock powers for that skill as appropriate for his number of ranks in that skill.

Side Gig (Ex)

Also at 2nd level, an s-class intern realizes that, to make ends meet, he needs to burn the midnight oil. He takes on a side gig; a means by which he makes some connections outside of his day job and actually becomes moderately recognized for the 8-10 extra hours a day he puts into all this writing, I mean his job as an adventurer.

When the intern enters a settlement, or remains in the same settlement for a full week, he can attempt a Diplomacy check in place of Craft or Profession to earn a living. The intern gains a bonus on this check equal to half his class level (minimum 1), or his full intern level if he chose Diplomacy with build competency.

This check represents the intern completing small jobs for a few coin here and there while his party does literally anything else and finally leaves him alone for two seconds during his only time off.

Clientele: An s-class intern’s side gig Diplomacy check can also introduce him to a potential client looking to complete a job related to his party’s current adventure. Jobs of this nature include, but are not limited to:

Capturing or killing a criminal who escaped the law by hiding out at the intern’s current destination.
Safeguarding a relic to be placed at the bottom of an abandoned ruin the intern and his allies are planning to explore.
Seeking out a family heirloom that was stolen or thought lost.
Finding and killing members of a specific faction or culture.

Such jobs do require the intern to speak openly about his work in order to garner interest, at least with his potential clients. The need to make rent ensures the intern is good about finding work that doesn’t interfere with their party’s current goals. If ever a circumstance would arise that a potential client offers a side gig that could draw the intern away or delay their party for more than a few hours at a time, the intern must figure out how to reassure his allies that it’s vaguely relevant without also cutting them in on his own earnings.

Niche

By 5th level, an s-class intern has found his niche side gig; the jobs that line up best with his availability (with only a modicum of shuffling work around here and there), and he begins to put focus on those jobs over other potential gigs. At 5th level, the intern chooses one of the following options. Once chosen, the intern cannot change his niche without spending one week of downtime and at least 100 gp per intern level to put out the word that his attention span is nonexistent and he’s now trying yet another thing.

Assassination, bounty, escort, labor, muscle, protection, theft

While working a side gig that relates to his niche, an s-class intern gains a +1 bonus on attack rolls and damage rolls. This bonus increases by +1 at 9th, 13th, and 17th level.

At 19th level, while working a side gig that relates to his niche, any attacks made by the intern automatically confirm all critical threats and have their damage multiplier increased by 1 (x2 becomes x3, for example). In addition, the intern is able to find ways to declare his current situation a related side gig as a swift action, such as asking a nearby ally if they’ll pay him to kill his current target, or suggesting that he is protecting a specific NPC who just happens to be there as well. Such declarations can, and often do, stretch reasonable bounds and credulity. But who cares by this point? He needs the money, Melnister, and we all know you aren’t going to give it to him.

Job Experience

Along with his niche, an s-class intern continues his training while on various side gigs. This helps him remain sharp and keeps him competitive with other interns, because nothing drives productivity like a little friendly competition… And pizza, and the occasional mandatory happy hour when you should be driving to your next job.

At 5th level, the intern gains the job experience benefit of his chosen niche. This benefit does not change if the intern later changes his niche. Instead, the intern can choose additional job experience options, from the same or a different niche at 9th, 13th, and 17th level. When he does, the intern gains the next available benefit in that niche (he cannot pick and choose options within a given niche). At 19th level, he gains two benefits instead.

A full list of job experience options can be found at the end of this section.

Determination (Ex)

At 4th level, an s-class intern realizes only he can really protect himself in the event he gets into danger. When he has taken more than half his total hit points in damage, the intern can receive the non-magical benefits of cure moderate wounds as an immediate action, using his intern level as the caster level for the effect. The intern can benefit from his determination once per day at 3rd level plus one additional time per day every 3 levels thereafter, to a maximum of 6 times per day at 19th level.

At 7th level, determination functions as cure serious wounds instead; and at 10th level, it functions as cure critical wounds.

Responsible (Ex)

At 3rd level, an s-class intern is given additional responsibilities within his group. He gains Expert Packing Method DLC as a bonus feat, and his allies gain a +1 morale bonus on the next skill check they make after the intern spends at least 2 full rounds helping them to prepare (this time can be spent in the morning, when a wizard would prepare his spells). This bonus increases by +1 at 6th level and every 3 levels thereafter, to a maximum of +6 at 18th level.

Individual Development Plan

At 3rd level, an s-class intern can choose a class ability possessed by one of his allies at the beginning of each day.

While he is within 10 feet of that ally and able to see and hear them, the intern can use the chosen ability a number of times per day up to half his intern level + his Intelligence modifier as if he were a member of the same class.

If an s-class intern chooses the ability to cast spells, he can only cast spells he has seen his chosen ally cast since the last time that ally regained spells.

If the ability learned with individual development plan is already limited, the intern uses whichever is the lower value. For example, a 3rd-level intern could gain smite 1/day, sneak attack +2d6, or cast burning hands, provided his ally has cast that spell recently.

Self-Paced Study (Ex)

At 4th level, when an s-class intern sets his individual development plan or secondment (see below), he also chooses a feat that could improve that class feature and gains it. He only gains the benefits of that feat while he has the class feature. When he doesn’t have a prerequisite class feature, or if there is no feat to improve it, the intern gains the benefits of and counts as having Improved Initiative and Iron Will instead.

At 7th and 17th level, the intern gains an additional feat in this way, or gains the benefits of Great Fortitude and Lightning Reflexes instead (choose one each time).

Action-Oriented (Ex)

Starting at 5th level, an s-class intern that observes one of his allies use a full-attack action can mimic that action exactly on his next turn if the weapons he wields would allow him to do so. The intern uses his ability scores in place of that ally’s.

Gap Analysis (Ex)

At 5th level, when an ally the intern can see and hear fails an attack roll, ability check, skill check, or saving throw, the intern can use follow the lead to attempt the same task before the end of his next turn with a bonus equal to his Intelligence modifier.

Job Shadowing (Su)

At 7th level, an s-class intern can use the ability he gained with individual development plan while standing no more than 30 feet from his ally. The intern must still be able to see and hear his ally the first time he or the ally uses that ability during the day.

The distance at which the intern can stand away from his chosen ally increases to 60 feet at 13th level, and 100 feet at 19th level.

Secondment (Ex)

At 11th level, an s-class intern can choose 1 class in which neither he nor his allies have levels. Once this choice is made, it can’t be changed, even if one of the intern’s allies later gains levels in the chosen class. He can choose a non-spellcasting ability from that class as his individual development plan each morning. Classes with progressive abilities (such as armor training, bloodline powers, or cleric domains) grant the highest progression available to a character of that level.

The intern is allowed to choose an unchained rogue’s sneak attack or finesse training with secondment if none of his allies are rogues or members of another class that counts as rogue.

Job Rotation (Ex)

At 17th level, an s-class intern can change his individual development plan from one ally to another (or to his secondment) as a full-round action once per day. If the new ally is a spellcaster, the intern can cast any spells that ally has cast since the start of the day.

This ability can grant the intern more uses of a set of abilities than normal. For example, if the intern used all of the rounds of rage granted him by his barbarian ally, he can then switch to using the paladin’s smite evil 6/day.

Experienced Intern (Ex)

At 20th level, an s-class intern has mastered his job.

He chooses one 20th level class feature from any of his allies’ classes (or his secondment) and gains that feature permanently. This does not apply to classes without a capstone ability that could be replaced by one of the options in that book we’re not allowed to call out by name, but which offers such things. If you need help finding it, it begins with C and ends with hronicle of Legends.

Side Gigs and Niches

The following side gigs are presented here without judgment, because work is work, and we all do what we must to make it these days. I see you. Your efforts are appreciated… Oh, and the intern does not have to meet any prerequisites of feats gained through his job experience.

Some side gigs count as being part of a class (in parentheses), so the intern can’t use them as options for his secondment. They function identically to the mercenary’s contract metier class feature, and a mercenary can choose any of these options as part of that feature or for their job training.

For each of the following side gigs, the intern gains job experience in order, so a 9th-level s-class intern who chooses his assassination for the second time with job training gains track, whereas a mercenary who chose protection at 5th level would only have one assassination experience, gaining sneak attack to complement his barrier focus.

Assassination (Rogue)

Assassins are about the quick kill, without care for the target or the circumstances that arise because of their actions.

As an s-class intern gains training in assassination, he gains the following benefits.

1. Sneak attack +1d6
2. Track (as a ranger of his intern level). This increases to his full intern level if he chose Survival with build competency.
3. Sneak attack +2d6
4. Poison use
5. Sneak attack +3d6
6. Poison immunity
Bounty

Bounty hunters seek a specific target to bring in, often, but not always alive. They differ from assassins in that they often work within the confines of the local law, so long as doing so suits them.

As an s-class intern gains training in bounty hunting, he gains the following benefits:

1. Step Up
2. Improved Grapple
3. Following Step
4. Improved Drag
5. Step up and Strike
6. Greater Grapple or Greater Drag
Creative

Creatives have looked at the world around them and decided they don’t actually need real income (they do).

They put their efforts into building their brand and acquiring as much recognition as they can stand.

As an s-class intern gains training in creativity, he gains the following benefits:

1. When the intern adventures for at least a week without entering or remaining in a settlement, he still makes his side gig roll to earn income. He can collect all income earned in this way upon entering a new settlement (independent of his roll for doing so).
2. Skill Focus (bluff or diplomacy)
3. Somebody pays the intern for their work through trade, rather than actual currency. Choose items worth no more than 1/4 of the character’s wealth by level. The intern gains those items. At each subsequent level, the intern gains the equivalent difference in new items, or can upgrade the items he already chose, accordingly.
4. The intern can attempt checks to earn income once per day instead of once per week.
5. The value of the intern’s trades becomes 1/3 instead (that’s actually better than before, even though 3 is less than 4).
6. Choose a class associated with the intern’s creative endeavors and a progressive class feature that class gains at 1st- through 5th-level. The intern counts as a 5th-level member of that class for the purpose of gaining or progressing the chosen class feature. This otherwise functions as the monk’s robes magic item.
Delivery (Inquisitor, Monk)

Deliverers are trusted with items that need to be taken from one location to another within a reasonable amount of time. A. Reasonable. Amount. Of. Time. They will sometimes receive tips for efficient and expedient service, assuming the recipient believes in such things.

As an s-class intern gains training in delivery, he gains the following benefits.

1. +10-foot enhancement bonus to speed or teamwork feat.
2. Solo tactics (as an inquisitor of his intern level.)
3. Cunning initiative (as an inquisitor of his intern level.) or teamwork feat.
4. +10-foot enhancement bonus to speed (up to +20 total) or teamwork feat.
5. Teamwork feat.
6. +10-foot enhancement bonus to speed (up to +30 total) or teamwork feat.
Escort (Bard)

An intern with an escort side gig acts as entertainment for caravans or affluent individuals, keeping them company when they’re away from home or just feeling down. While they don’t mind getting their blade dirty, these interns do what they can to avoid such a turn of events.

As an s-class intern gains training in escorting, he gains the following benefits:

1. Knowledge (local) as a class skill and the benefit of build competency with that skill.
2. Endurance and Toughness
3. Fascinate (as a bard of his intern level).
4. Evasion
5. Soothing performance (as a bard of his intern level).
6. Improved evasion
Labor

Laborers are skilled craftsmen and work horses, whose understanding of a profession or craft gets them by. It draws the attention of potential clients who have seen their mark and the quality of their work.

As an s-class intern gains training in labor, he gains the following benefits:

1. Skill Focus (one craft or profession). The intern can substitute Charisma in place of Intelligence or Wisdom on these checks.
2. Master Craftsman or Prodigy (+2 bonus on two of any Craft or Profession, +4 at 10 ranks).
3. Always take 10 on a Craft or Profession skill check for which the intern has Skill Focus. Take 20 1/day.
4. The intern can attempt checks to earn income once per day instead of once per week.
5. Take 20 2/day.
6. The intern can spend 1 minute to change his Skill Focus benefits gained with this metier once per day.
Moonlighter (Vigilante)

Moonlighters are interns who took that role to play down what they actually do. To them, interning is the side gig.

As an s-class intern gains training in moonlilghting, he gains the following benefits.

1. The intern selects any one Intelligence-, Wisdom-, or Charisma-based skill other than Perception or Use Magic Device. Whenever the intern is doing anything unrelated to his adventuring party, he receives a +4 circumstance bonus on checks with the selected skill. At 5th level and every 4 levels thereafter, he can select another skill (with the same restrictions) to gain this bonus.
2. The intern can use Stealth to hide even when being observed. As long as he is within 10 feet of dim light (his own shadow doesn’t count) or a larger creature, he can hide without anything to actually hide behind.
3. The intern gains one of the following feats as a bonus feat: Blustering Bluff, But a Scratch, Call Truce, Confabulist, Criminal Reputation, Cutting Humiliation, Esoteric Linguistics, Intoxicating Flattery, Ironclad Logic, Nerve-Racking Negotiator, Orator, Persuasive Bribery, Play to the Crowd, Quick Favor, Rhetorical Flourish, Sense Assumptions, Sense Relationships, or Street Smarts. He must meet the feat’s prerequisites.
4. Once per day, the intern can state a plan of action. All allies within 30 feet that can hear him gain a +2 morale bonus on saving throws against fear effects and are immune to being demoralized. They also gain a +1 morale bonus on skill checks or combat maneuver checks of the intern’s choice. The benefits last for 1 round per intern level.
5. The intern sits at the center of a network of other interns, granting him access to the latest scuttlebutt with baffling speed. Whenever the intern is presented with a topic about which he would normally need to spend 1d4 hours to gather information, he must spend only 1d2 hours instead. If he gathers the information in an area where he’s earned income, he must instead spend only 1d4 × 10 minutes, and if he beats the DC to gather a piece of information by 20 or more, he knows that piece of information without spending any time at all; he has simply already heard that gossip. This ability doesn’t allow him to gather information that isn’t available to his network, as determined by the GM.
6. The intern gains Swift Aid as a bonus feat, ignoring its prerequisites. Additionally, the intern can use the feat as a standard action, in which case it applies to every ally adjacent to the intern. At 10th level, the intern can increase the bonus provided to one ally by this feat to +2 by using the aid another action as a move action rather than as a swift action.
Muscle (Barbarian)

Interns who act as the muscle for a side gig work collections, taking coin or other predetermined payment.

Should that payment not be made within a reasonable amount of time, the muscle is expected to resolve the situation by any means necessary.

As an s-class intern gains training in muscle, he gains the following benefits:

1. Rage (as a barbarian, a number of rounds per day equal to the intern’s Charisma bonus).
2. Dazzling Display, rage +2 rounds
3. Rage power, rage +2 rounds
4. Shatter Defenses, rage +2 rounds
5. Rage power, rage +2 rounds
6. Deadly Stroke (does not require Greater Weapon Focus), rage +2 rounds
Protection (Barrier Sentinel LoT)

Interns distinguish work as muscle from that of protection with the tasks they perform. While muscle goes out and works on behalf of the client, protectors stay close and guard the client from potential harm.

As an s-class intern gains training in protection, he gains the following benefits:

1. The intern gains proficiency in heavy armor, and can use barrier focus as a barrier sentinel, a number of rounds per day equal to his Charisma bonus.
2. Barrier focus +2 rounds, Bodyguard: When an adjacent ally is attacked, the intern may use an attack of opportunity to attempt the aid another action to improve his ally’s AC. He may not use the aid another action to improve his ally’s attack roll with the attack.
3. Barrier focus +2 rounds, and the intern gains his choice of Tower Shield Proficiency or a barrier sentinel focus power.
4. Barrier focus +2 rounds, In Harm’s Way: While using the aid another action to improve an adjacent ally’s AC, the intern can intercept a successful attack against that ally as an immediate action, taking full damage from that attack and any associated effects (bleed, poison, etc.). A creature cannot benefit from this feat more than once per attack.
5. Barrier focus +2 rounds, focus power
6. Barrier focus +2 rounds, and the intern becomes immune to enchantment spells and effects.
Theft

Thieves are to objects as bounty hunters are to creatures.

These interns are hired to find and procure items for their clients. While some fashion themselves relic hunters and historians, many don’t even bother with those semantics.

As an s-class intern gains training in theft, he gains the following benefits:

1. The intern adds Sleight of Hand to his list of class skills and can use Sleight of Hand in place of a combat maneuver check to steal.
2. Improved Disarm, Improved Steal, or Skill Focus (sleight of hand)
3. The penalty for attempting a Sleight of Hand check (including drawing a hidden weapon) as a move action is reduced to –10.
4. The intern can attempt a steal combat maneuver as his first attack each round (whether made as a standard action or as part of a full-attack action).
5. If the intern succeeds at a disarm or steal combat maneuver, he can make an attack roll against a creature within 5 feet as a free action.
6. If the intern confirms a critical hit with an attack, he can also attempt a disarm or steal combat maneuver as an immediate action (using his highest attack bonus). If the attack was ranged, the dropped or stolen object falls unattended to the ground.
Feats

The following feats are summarized for ease of reference here. For the full text of each, refer to its original source.

Blustering Bluff

Prerequisite(s): Cha 13, Bluff 1 rank, Intimidate 1 rank.

Benefit(s): When using Bluff to fool a foe, you can bully that person to reduce the penalty for telling an unlikely or farfetched lie by 5. If you do so and your check would not have succeeded otherwise, after 1d6×10 minutes, the person you fooled realizes you bullied him into believing a lie, treats you as unfriendly, and might report you or take other actions against you.

Normal: The penalty for telling unlikely lies is –5, and the penalty for telling far-fetched lies is –10.

But a Scratch

Prerequisite(s): Cha 13, Bluff 4 ranks.

Benefit(s): When an opponent confirms a critical hit against you with a melee weapon, you can attempt a special Bluff check against that opponent as an immediate action. The DC of this check is the same as the DC to demoralize the opponent with the Intimidate skill. If you are successful, the attacking opponent is shaken for 1 round as if you had successfully demoralized it with Intimidate.

Exceeding the DC by 5 or more does not add to the shaken condition’s duration. If you fail the special Bluff check granted by this feat, you can attempt it against opponents who saw you attempt the earlier check and fail, but you take a –2 cumulative penalty on that Bluff check and any subsequent Bluff checks attempted in conjunction with this feat against those opponents for 24 hours.

Call Truce

Prerequisite(s): Cha 15, Persuasive, Diplomacy 5 ranks.

Benefit(s): While in combat, as a 1-round action (as if it were a spell with a 1-round casting time, you can call for a truce with any creatures that have an Intelligence score of 4 or greater and can understand you. When doing so, you can’t be wielding a weapon or threatening implement, such as a charged spell, wand, or anything else the creatures you are entreating might consider threatening. You must also be in plain sight of most the creatures you are entreating.

Once you’ve called for a truce, if any of your allies attack or take any threatening action against those you are entreating before the start of your next turn, your call is unsuccessful.

At the start of your next turn, attempt a single Diplomacy check (DC = 30 + the Charisma modifier of the creature with the highest Charisma modifier in the opposing group). If you are successful, combat ceases for 1 minute, or until any creature in the opposing group is threatened or attacked.

If you fail the check by 5 or more, you cannot use Diplomacy again with any creature you attempted to entreat for 1d4 hours. If anyone in your group instead plans to use the parley to gain a combat advantage, the opponents can attempt a Sense Motive check against each such member of your group to get a hunch, with a DC equal to either 20 or the result of that character’s Bluff check, whichever is higher.

Special: If the parley would inherently result in the opponents surrendering or losing, if the opponents are mind-controlled or fanatics, or if there are other appropriate circumstances at the GM’s discretion, you might not be able to use this feat. For instance, if the opponents’ main advantage over your group comes from a short-duration spell that would end during a parley (see Calling for a Cease-Fire), you cannot use this feat. Circumstances could potentially increase the check’s DC by 5, 10, or even up to 20.

Confabulist

Prerequisite(s): Bluff 9 ranks, Sense Motive 9 ranks.

Benefit(s): When you fail to deceive someone with a Bluff check, you can immediately attempt another version of the same basic deception against that creature at a –5 penalty by downplaying the failed Bluff and quickly moving on to another one. You cannot use this ability if the first Bluff was so egregious that further checks would have been impossible (as per the Bluff skill). If you fail the second attempt, you cannot retry the Bluff check and all further attempts to perpetrate that particular deception are impossible.

Normal: When you fail a Bluff check against a creature, that creature is innately suspicious. You take a –10 penalty on future attempts to deceive that creature, or at the GM’s discretion, such attempts may be impossible.

Criminal Reputation

Prerequisite(s): Diplomacy 5 ranks, Intimidate 5 ranks.

Benefit(s): You gain a +2 bonus on Diplomacy and Intimidate checks when interacting with criminals, whether they’re individual thieves and cutpurses or criminal organizations.

If you have 10 or more ranks in one of these skills, the bonus increases to +4 for that skill.

These bonuses do not stack with those granted by Persuasive, but this feat counts as Persuasive for the purposes of feats and other rules elements with Persuasive as a prerequisite.

Cutting Humiliation

Prerequisite(s): Persuasive, Intimidate 5 ranks.

Benefit(s): When you successfully demoralize a target by using a verbal Intimidate check in a social situation (rather than an Intimidate check you can make via an ability such as Dazzling Display or Enforcer), you can instead humiliate the target, causing it to take a –2 penalty on Charismabased skill checks and Charisma ability checks for 1 hour + 1 additional hour for every 5 by which the result of your check exceeds the DC. The target can remove the effect early by taking 10 minutes to compose herself. If you fail this check, any creature who witnessed the failure is immune to your humiliation from this feat for 24 hours. If you fail by 5 or more, you become humiliated for 1 hour instead of your target.

Esoteric Linguistics

Prerequisite(s): Skill Focus (Linguistics).

Benefit(s): You can attempt a Linguistics check in place of a Use Magic Device check to activate a scroll, or in place of a Spellcraft check to identify a scroll. You must still have (or emulate) the ability score required to cast a spell of the desired level, and you cannot use Linguistics on the check to emulate the required ability score.

Intoxicating Flattery

Prerequisite(s): Deceitful, Bluff 5 ranks.

Benefit(s): You can flatter a creature in a protracted interaction (taking at least 1 minute) to bestow in them an inflated sense of self worth that muddles their judgment.

At the end of the tirade of flattery, attempt a Bluff check against a DC equal to 10 + the creature’s HD + the creature’s Wisdom modifier or equal to 10 + the creature’s Sense Motive modifier, whichever is higher. If you succeed, the target takes a –2 penalty on Will saving throws, Wisdombased skill checks, and Wisdom ability checks for 1 hour plus an additional hour for every 5 by which your result exceeds the DC. The target can remove the effect early by taking 10 minutes to compose herself. If you fail this check, any creature who witnesses the failure is immune to your flattery from this feat for 24 hours. If you fail by 5 or more, the target’s attitude toward you decreases by 1 step.

Ironclad Logic

Prerequisite(s): Int 19, Diplomacy 3 ranks.

Benefit(s): You gain a +4 bonus on Diplomacy checks whenever you add your Charisma modifier on those checks. If you have at least 10 ranks in Diplomacy and an Intelligence score of 27 or more, this bonus increases to +8.

This bonus doesn’t stack with the bonus from Skill Focus (Diplomacy), but this feat counts as Skill Focus (Diplomacy) for the purpose of feats and other elements with Skill Focus (Diplomacy) as a prerequisite. In verbal duels, when using tactics to which you assigned an Intelligence-based skill, you can add your Intelligence modifier instead of your Charisma modifier to the associated skill check.

Nerve-Racking Negotiator

Prerequisite(s): Persuasive.

Benefit(s): When you successfully use the Intimidate skill to force an opponent to act friendly toward you, the target must attempt a Will save once the intimidation wears off. The DC is equal to 10 + your number of ranks in Intimidate.

If the target fails this save, after the intimidation period expires, the target counts as having the same attitude toward you as it initially did (usually indifferent) and will not report you to the authorities for intimidating it.

Normal: The target of a successful Intimidate check is unfriendly to you and potentially reports you to the authorities after the duration ends.

Orator

Prerequisite(s): Skill Focus (Linguistics).

Benefit(s): You can use a Linguistics check in place of a Bluff check to tell a falsehood or conceal information, in place of a Diplomacy check to change the attitude of a creature, or in place of an Intimidate check to force a creature to cooperate. You must deliver your attempt in a language the target understands.

Persuasive Bribery

Prerequisite(s): Persuasive.

Benefit(s): You gain a +2 bonus on Diplomacy checks when attempting to bribe someone and on Diplomacy or Charisma checks to bargain with a conjured creature (such as with planar ally or planar binding), in addition to any bonus granted by the bribe itself. The first time someone refuses a bribe you offer, that person’s attitude toward you doesn’t worsen, even if the offer would normally offend the person.

Play to the Crowd

Prerequisite(s): Int 19, Ironclad Logic, Diplomacy 5 ranks, Sense Motive 5 ranks.

Benefit(s): When you use Diplomacy to change the attitude of a character, you can first attempt a Sense Motive check against that NPC to get a hunch, to determine whether the 8 character is under the influence of an enchantment, to use Sense Assumptions, or to determine biases for a verbal duel. If you succeed at the Sense Motive check, you gain a +2 bonus on the Diplomacy check, and if you learned any biases for a verbal duel, you learn one additional bias of your choice. You do not worsen an NPC’s attitude if you fail a Diplomacy check by 5 or more.

Quick Favor

Prerequisite(s): Persuasive.

Benefit(s): Once per day, you can decrease the time required for a Diplomacy check to gather information to 4d10 minutes when you use Diplomacy to gather information again just after you previously gathered information there (whether or not the previous attempt was successful).

Normal: You must spend 1d4 hours to gather information using Diplomacy.

Rhetorical Flourish

Prerequisite(s): Cha 13, Persuasive.

Benefit(s): When using the Diplomacy skill to make a request or change a creature’s attitude, you can use verbal misdirection. To do so, make a Bluff check against that creature. If you succeed, you gain a +4 bonus on your next Diplomacy check against that creature if the check is made within the next minute. If you fail by 5 or more, you instead take a –2 penalty on your next Diplomacy check against that creature.

Alternatively, you can use this feat to retry a single failed Diplomacy check against a creature. You take a –4 penalty on your Bluff check when using Rhetorical Flourish in this way. If you succeed, rather than gaining this feat’s normal bonus, you can retry your last Diplomacy check against the creature if that check was made in the past minute.

Sense Assumptions

Prerequisite(s): Sense Motive 3 ranks.

Benefit(s): You can attempt a Sense Motive check to intuit some of another person’s assumptions after 1 minute of conversation. The DC equals 20, or 10 + the target’s Bluff modifier, whichever is higher. If you succeed, you learn whether or not a falsehood of your choice related to the topic of conversation would impose a penalty on Bluff checks to convince the target of that falsehood’s truth.

If you fail by 4 or less, you learn nothing. If you fail by 5 or more, the target realizes you are trying to glean information from it. You can retry this check, but the DC increases by 5 for each previous failure on this check against that target.

Sense Relationships

Prerequisite(s): Street Smarts.

Benefit(s): After 1 minute or more of interaction or observation, you can attempt a DC 20 Sense Motive check to get a hunch in order to intuit the relationship between any two creatures interacting with one another.

If you don’t understand the language they are speaking, you take a –5 penalty on the check, and if the creatures are a different type than you, you take an additional –5 penalty on the check.

If you succeed at this check by 5 or more, for the next hour, you gain a +2 bonus on Bluff checks to lie about one of the creatures to the other and on Diplomacy checks to request that one act against the other. If you fail the check, you cannot attempt this ability on the same creatures again until you gain an additional rank in Sense Motive.

Street Smarts

Benefit(s): You get a +2 bonus on Knowledge (local) and Sense Motive checks, and Knowledge (local) is always a class skill for you. If you have 10 or more ranks in one of these skills, the bonus increases to +4 for that skill. The bonus on Sense Motive checks doesn’t stack with Alertness.
